summary: A recursive DNS resolver in TypeScript on node:dgram and node:net, zero runtime dependencies, and node:dns is NOT used for resolution (only in the opt-in live test as an independent check). Stage 1, src/wire.ts: the RFC 1035 wire format -- 12-byte header with QR/opcode/AA/TC/RD/RA/rcode, question and the three record sections, record types A, AAAA (RFC 5952 text form), NS, CNAME, SOA, MX, TXT (latin1 so every byte survives), PTR, and every other type (incl. OPT) kept as raw rdata (RFC 3597). Names are strings without the trailing dot with presentation escapes (\. and \DDD) so a label containing a dot is never two labels; comparison is ASCII case-insensitive and label by label (isSubdomain). Decoding is bounds checked everywhere (Reader.need), a compression pointer must point strictly before the labels being read (so pointer targets strictly decrease and decoding always ends) and a name may follow at most MAX_POINTER_JUMPS = 32 pointers; names over 255 bytes, reserved label types and an rdlength that does not match what the rdata uses are rejected; every failure is a WireError. Encoding compresses names case-insensitively. Stage 2, src/resolver.ts + src/transport.ts: iterative resolution from the embedded IANA root hints (src/root-hints.ts, copied 2026-11-21 from named.root dated November 12, 2026): referrals with glue, out-of-bailiwick NS lookups as nested resolutions with a depth limit, CNAME chains with a limit of 8 links, NXDOMAIN and NODATA with the SOA, lame or upward referrals skipped, SERVFAIL/REFUSED/timeouts/garbage move on to the next server, TC=1 retried over TCP with the 2-byte length prefix, a budget of 60 upstream queries per resolution. Spoofing defences: a fresh UDP socket per query on a random source port picked with crypto.randomInt (10000-65535), a random 16-bit ID, and a reply is only accepted from the exact address and port with QR set, our ID and our exact question; anything else is ignored and we keep waiting. Bailiwick: a server asked about zone Z can only teach records at or below Z; everything else is dropped before the cache. Stage 3, src/cache.ts + src/server.ts + src/index.ts: a TTL cache of whole RRsets (smallest TTL of the set, capped at maxTtl, TTL 0 never cached, injected clock), negative caching per RFC 2308 (NXDOMAIN per name, NODATA per name and type, TTL = min(SOA TTL, SOA minimum), capped at 3 hours, not cached without an SOA), a two-level rank so referral data (NS, glue) never overwrites an answer and is never returned as one; a UDP + TCP stub server on 127.0.0.1 (configurable port, refuses a non-loopback bind unless ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1) that answers with RA=1, copies ID and RD, FORMERR for undecodable bodies, NOTIMP for other opcodes/classes/ANY/AXFR, drops QR=1 packets, and truncates UDP answers over 512 bytes with TC=1; a CLI with a resolve command that prints every step. Tests never need the internet: a fake network of in-process authoritative servers (UDP and TCP on the same ephemeral loopback port) serving fixture zones with documentation addresses, mapped through the resolver's route hook. Interop: packets captured from Windows nslookup.exe are decoded and answered in the normal suite; an opt-in run of nslookup.exe against the stub server passes (finding: this nslookup build ignores -port, so it needs port 53). The opt-in LIVE_DNS=1 test resolves real names from the real root servers and passed on 2026-11-21.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek DNS resolver khud likha hai, TypeScript mein, sirf node:dgram aur node:net par -- node:dns resolution ke liye use nahi kiya, kyunki point hi yahi tha. Yeh binary wire format khud parse karta hai (name compression ke saath, loop protection ke saath), root servers se shuru karke referrals follow karta hai, glue aur out-of-bailiwick NS lookups, CNAME chains, NXDOMAIN aur NODATA handle karta hai, truncated reply par TCP par retry karta hai, aur TTL wala cache rakhta hai jismein negative caching bhi hai. Upar ek chhota stub server hai 127.0.0.1 par, jisse nslookup seedha baat karta hai. Tests internet ke bina chalte hain ek fake authoritative network par, aur ek opt-in live test real root servers se resolve karta hai.
pitch.explain_2min:
Project A6 ke teen hisse hain.

Pehla, src/wire.ts: DNS message binary hai -- 12 byte ka header (ID, flags QR/AA/TC/RD/RA, rcode, chaar counts), phir question aur teen record sections. Naam labels mein hote hain (length byte + bytes), aur jagah bachane ke liye ek naam ka suffix pehle aaye naam ki taraf 2-byte pointer ban sakta hai. Yeh pointer attacker ke haath mein hai, toh decode mein do rules hain: pointer hamesha current labels se PEECHE point kare (targets strictly ghatte hain, toh loop impossible) aur ek naam max 32 pointers follow kare. Har read bounds checked hai; garbage packet sirf WireError deta hai -- 6000 random aur bit-flipped packets ke fuzz test se dikhaya.

Doosra, src/resolver.ts aur src/transport.ts: resolve(name, type) cache dekhta hai, phir sabse nazdeeki known zone cut se (ya root hints se) poochta hai RD=0 ke saath. Jawab answer, CNAME, referral, NXDOMAIN ya NODATA hota hai. Referral mein glue ho toh use karo, nahi toh NS ka naam pehle khud resolve karo (nested lookup, depth limit ke saath). Timeout, SERVFAIL, REFUSED, garbage, lame referral -- sab par agla server. TC bit aaye toh wahi query TCP par, 2-byte length prefix ke saath. Har UDP query naye socket se jaati hai, random port aur random ID ke saath, aur reply tabhi maani jaati hai jab address, port, ID aur question sab match karein -- yeh Kaminsky-style spoofing ka jawab hai. Aur bailiwick: jis server se zone Z ke baare mein poocha, uski sirf Z ke andar wali records maani jaati hain.

Teesra, src/cache.ts aur src/server.ts: RRset ka cache (sabse chhota TTL, injected clock), RFC 2308 negative caching (SOA minimum se), referral data ka kam rank. Stub server UDP aur TCP dono par, loopback only, 512 byte se bada UDP jawab TC=1 ke saath.

Testing: fake authoritative servers loopback ports par, documentation IPs ke saath, resolver ke route hook se map. Interop nslookup.exe ke captured packets se, aur mutation checks se tests ki taakat napi.
pitch.deep_5min:
Main ek query ki poori journey batata hoon: user nslookup www.alpha.test chalata hai.

1. Stub server (src/server.ts) ko UDP packet milta hai. Pehle decodeHeader -- 12 byte bhi nahi hain toh drop, kyunki ID ke bina jawab kisko doge. QR=1 hai (yeh toh response hai) toh bhi drop, warna do servers aapas mein ping-pong kar sakte hain. Body decode na ho toh FORMERR usi ID ke saath. Opcode QUERY nahi, class IN nahi, ya ANY/AXFR hai toh NOTIMP. Exactly ek question chahiye, warna FORMERR.

2. Resolver.resolve chalta hai ek budget ke saath: poori resolution mein max 60 upstream queries, nested lookups mila ke. Yeh budget aur maxDepth hi delegation loops ko SERVFAIL mein khatam karte hain, hang mein nahi.

3. resolveOne pehle cache dekhta hai: answer rank ka RRset, phir negative entry (NXDOMAIN poore naam ke liye, NODATA naam+type ke liye), phir cached CNAME. Miss hua toh closestServers: naam se upar chalte hue pehla ancestor jiska NS set aur kam se kam ek address cache mein ho. Kuch nahi toh root hints -- woh src/root-hints.ts mein hain, IANA ki named.root file se copy, date ke saath.

4. askZone: servers shuffle karke ek ek se poochna. exchange() naya UDP socket random port par bind karta hai (crypto.randomInt, OS par nahi chhoda), random ID, RD=0. Reply sirf tab maani jaati hai jab woh usi IP aur port se aaye, QR set ho, ID same ho, aur question exactly wahi echo kare. Galat reply ignore -- query fail nahi hoti, kyunki warna attacker galat guess bhej ke har lookup fail kara sakta. TC=1 aaye toh wahi server, TCP par, length prefix ke saath.

5. classify: yeh dil hai. Pehle bailiwick filter -- zone Z ke server ki sirf Z ke andar ki records. Phir NXDOMAIN (SOA ke saath negative cache), direct answer (cache, done), CNAME (cache, caller target follow karega, max 8 links), referral (NS jo zone se neeche aur naam ke upar ho; upar ya side mein point kare toh lame, agla server), aur warna NODATA.

6. Referral par glue sirf tab use hota hai jab woh bhejne wale zone ke andar ho. test TLD server ns.hoster.example ka glue bheje toh woh drop -- hum example TLD se khud poochte hain. Glue aur NS 'referral' rank par cache hote hain: kisi answer ko overwrite nahi karte aur client ko answer ke taur par kabhi nahi diye jaate.

7. Answer stub server tak lautta hai: RA=1, ID aur RD copy, answer section mein CNAME chain + final RRset, negative mein SOA authority mein. 512 byte se bada UDP jawab TC=1 aur khaali sections ke saath, client TCP par dobara poochta hai.

Sabse mushkil decisions: pehla, tests ko internet se alag rakhna. Glue mein sirf IP hota hai, port nahi, toh fake network ke liye ek route hook banaya: documentation IP (192.0.2.x) -> loopback port. Zones real jaisi dikhti hain aur production mein route identity hai port 53 ke saath. Doosra, malformed input: har read bounds-checked aur ek hi error type, aur pointer ke do alag rules jinhe alag alag test kiya. Teesra, honesty: mutation checks se pata chala ki kaunsa rule kisi test se pakda nahi gaya, aur woh README mein likha hai. Ek real finding bhi mili: is Windows build ka nslookup -port ko ignore karta hai, isliye live interop port 53 par opt-in hai.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough:
src/wire.ts: Message types, Reader (bounds-checked u8/u16/u32/bytes/name), readName (compression decode, backwards-only rule, 32-pointer cap, 255-byte limit), readRData per type with rdlength check, Writer with case-insensitive compression, encodeMessage/decodeMessage/decodeHeader, name helpers canonicalName, isSubdomain, parentName.

src/transport.ts: queryUdp (fresh socket, random port, random ID, source/ID/question checks, ignore-and-keep-waiting), queryTcp (2-byte length prefix), LengthPrefixedReader (TCP framing, shared with the server), matchesQuery.

src/root-hints.ts: ROOT_HINTS, 13 root servers with source and date.

src/resolver.ts: Resolver.resolve -> resolveChain (CNAME limit) -> resolveOne (cache, closestServers, referral loop) -> askZone (server order, budget, next server on failure) -> exchange (UDP, TC -> TCP) -> classify (bailiwick filter, NXDOMAIN, answer, CNAME, referral with glue, lame, NODATA), serversFor (glue, cache, nested NS lookup with maxDepth).

src/cache.ts: Cache with positive RRsets (rank referral/answer), negative entries (NXDOMAIN per name, NODATA per name+type), TTL countdown, caps, eviction by age.

src/server.ts: DnsServer, UDP + TCP on one port, loopback guard, handle() with FORMERR/NOTIMP/QR-drop/TC rules, stats.

src/index.ts: CLI, serve or resolve with trace.

test/fakenet.ts + test/fixtures.ts: the fake internet -- FakeServer (authoritative logic, hooks for misbehaviour, query log) and the fixture zone tree.
difficult_decisions: Tests bina internet: fake authoritative servers loopback par, aur resolver ka route hook jo documentation IP ko loopback port par map karta hai. Real referral ke glue mein port nahi hota, isliye yeh 'routing table' chahiye thi; production mein route identity hai port 53 ke saath.

Compression pointer ke do alag rules: backwards-only (loop impossible) aur 32-pointer cap (lambi chain ka kaam bounded). Dono ko alag tests se prove kiya, taaki ek rule hatane par doosra use chhupa na de.
Galat UDP reply ko ignore karna, fail nahi karna: warna off-path attacker galat guesses bhej ke har lookup fail kara deta. Query sirf timeout par khatam hoti hai.
Bailiwick zone ke hisaab se, aur glue sirf bhejne wale zone ke andar: Kaminsky ke 'extra records' wale hisse ka jawab. Referral data ko kam rank diya taaki woh answers ko kabhi overwrite na kare.
Sirf IPv4 transport aur EDNS nahi: scope chhota rakha; isliye stub server UDP par 512 byte tak hi bhejta hai aur bada jawab TC=1 se TCP par jaata hai.
Stub server loopback only, ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1 ke bina: open resolver amplification attacks mein use hota hai aur is mein na access control hai na rate limit.
biggest_challenges: Malformed packets: ek bhi unchecked read crash ya infinite loop de sakta tha. Har truncation offset aur 6000 random / bit-flipped packets ka fuzz test, aur sirf WireError ki guarantee.

Delegation loops (loop1.test <-> loop2.test, dono bina glue): nested NS lookups kabhi khatam na hote. Query budget aur depth limit ne SERVFAIL banaya; mutation checks ne dikhaya ki dono limits ko alag test chahiye.

Windows nslookup -port ko ignore karta hai: pehle interop test 'No response from server' de raha tha. 53 aur N dono par listener laga ke dikhaya ki packets sirf 53 par aate hain; live interop isliye port 53 par opt-in hai, aur captured packets normal suite mein.

Live test mein node:dns (c-ares) ne 127.0.0.1 ko server maana aur ECONNREFUSED diya; isliye cross-check ke liye OS getaddrinfo (dns.lookup) use kiya, aur MX/NXDOMAIN ka c-ares check sirf LIVE_DNS_CHECK_SERVER dene par.
failure_scenarios: Ek zone ka ek server mara hua: timeout ke baad agla server; saare mare hue toh har ek ko ek baar try karke SERVFAIL, hang nahi.
Server SERVFAIL/REFUSED ya garbage bheje: agla server. Garbage UDP reply ignore hoti hai aur query timeout tak intezaar karti hai.
Spoofed reply (galat ID, galat port, galat question): ignore, asli reply use hoti hai. Poisoned extra records doosre zone ke liye: bailiwick filter drop kar deta hai.
CNAME loop ya bahut lambi chain: 8 links ke baad SERVFAIL.
Lame delegation (server root ki taraf wapas refer kare): lame maana, agla server, aur koi nahi bacha toh SERVFAIL.
Outbound UDP 53 blocked network: live test fail hoga; resolver har server ko timeout ke baad chhodta hai aur budget se bounded rehta hai.
improvements: EDNS(0): bade UDP jawab (1232 bytes) taaki TCP fallback kam ho; aur stub client ka OPT samajhna.
IPv6 transport aur happy-eyeballs style server choice; abhi sirf IPv4.
Server selection by measured RTT (SRTT jaise BIND/Unbound) aur lame servers ko kuch der yaad rakhna.
Ek jaisi parallel queries ko jodna (in-flight dedupe) aur stub server par rate limiting / max concurrent.
Root priming (start par . NS poochna), QNAME minimisation (RFC 9156) privacy ke liye, aur 0x20 case randomisation se aur entropy.
DNSSEC validation -- spoofing ka asli jawab cryptographic signatures hain, random ports sirf mushkil banate hain.

learning_path.concept: DNS wire format and parsing untrusted binary input
steps: 1. Concept: DNS message = 12-byte header + question + answer/authority/additional sections, sab binary, big-endian.
2. Project need: har byte network se aata hai aur attacker ke control mein ho sakta hai; ek unchecked read crash ya galat parse deta hai.
3. Code/API: wire.ts decodeMessage, encodeMessage, decodeHeader, Reader (u8/u16/u32/bytes/need), readRData.
4. Detail: counts se koi array pre-size nahi hota; rdlength ko record type ke saath match karna (A = 4, AAAA = 16), rdata ke andar ka naam rdata ke bahar na jaaye.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/wire.test.ts -t fuzz
6. Interviewer next: fuzz test kya prove karta hai aur kya nahi? Truncated packet aur trailing bytes mein kya farq hai?
1. Concept: naam ka suffix pehle aaye naam ki taraf 2-byte pointer (top 2 bits 11, 14-bit offset) ban sakta hai.
2. Project need: packet chhota rehta hai, lekin pointer attacker ka hai -- self-pointer ya A -> B -> A loop decoder ko hamesha ke liye ghuma sakta hai.
3. Code/API: wire.ts readName (runStart, MAX_POINTER_JUMPS), Writer.name (suffix map, offset < 0x4000).
4. Detail: rule 1 pointer strictly peeche point kare (targets ghatte hain, loop impossible); rule 2 max 32 pointers (kaam bounded). Encode case-insensitive compress karta hai.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/wire.test.ts -t pointer
6. Interviewer next: sirf jump counter kaafi kyun nahi? Forward pointer allow karne mein kya risk hai?

learning_path.concept: Iterative resolution: referrals, glue, out-of-bailiwick NS
steps: 1. Concept: resolver root se shuru karke referrals follow karta hai: root -> TLD -> zone, har baar RD=0.
2. Project need: koi upstream recursive resolver nahi; poora rasta khud chalna hai.
3. Code/API: resolver.ts resolve, resolveChain, resolveOne, closestServers, askZone, classify, serversFor.
4. Detail: referral sirf neeche ki taraf valid; glue sirf bhejne wale zone ke andar; glue nahi toh NS host ka nested lookup maxDepth ke saath.
5. Demo: npm run build; node dist/index.js resolve www.wikipedia.org A (trace dekho), ya npx vitest run test/resolver.test.ts -t referral
6. Interviewer next: lame delegation kya hai? Glue ke bina in-zone NS host ho toh kya hota hai?

learning_path.concept: CNAME chains, NXDOMAIN, NODATA and the limits that stop loops
steps: 1. Concept: CNAME alias hai; NXDOMAIN = naam hi nahi; NODATA = naam hai, yeh type nahi.
2. Project need: chain doosre zone mein ja sakti hai, loop ho sakta hai, delegation loop bhi.
3. Code/API: resolveChain (maxCnameChain 8), askZone (maxQueries 60), serversFor (maxDepth 4), maxReferrals 16.
4. Detail: har limit SERVFAIL deti hai reason ke saath, hang nahi; budget nested lookups mein share hota hai.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/resolver.test.ts -t CNAME ; -t loop
6. Interviewer next: limit kitni rakhni chahiye aur kyun? Budget per resolution vs per query?

learning_path.concept: UDP transport, TC bit and TCP fallback
steps: 1. Concept: DNS pehle UDP; jawab bada ho toh server TC=1 bhejta hai aur client TCP par dobara poochta hai, har message 2-byte length prefix ke saath.
2. Project need: bina EDNS ke UDP 512 byte tak; bada TXT RRset TCP ke bina nahi aata.
3. Code/API: transport.ts queryUdp, queryTcp, LengthPrefixedReader, frameTcp; resolver.ts exchange; server.ts UDP_MAX_ANSWER.
4. Detail: wahi server, naya ID; server side TCP par pipelined aur split frames.
5. Demo: npx vitest run -t truncated
6. Interviewer next: EDNS(0) is mein kya badalta? TCP par spoofing kyun mushkil hai?
1. Concept: off-path attacker ko reply guess karni padti hai: ID aur source port; Kaminsky ne random non-existent names se har query ko nayi race banaya.
2. Project need: resolver ka cache poison hua toh har client galat IP par jaayega.
3. Code/API: transport.ts randomId, SOURCE_PORT_MIN, matchesQuery, onIgnored; resolver.ts classify (inZone filter).
4. Detail: galat reply ignore, fail nahi; zone Z ke server ki sirf Z ke andar ki records; referral data kam rank.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/resolver.test.ts -t spoof ; -t bailiwick
6. Interviewer next: DNSSEC is sab ko kaise badalta hai? 0x20 kya hai?

learning_path.concept: TTL cache, negative caching and ranking
steps: 1. Concept: har record ka TTL; RFC 2308 negative answers bhi cache hote hain SOA minimum se.
2. Project need: har lookup root se nahi; aur jo naam nahi hai use baar baar na poochna.
3. Code/API: cache.ts Cache.putRRset, getRRset, putNegative, getNegative, Rank, maxTtl, maxNegativeTtl, maxEntries.
4. Detail: RRset ka sabse chhota TTL; NXDOMAIN per naam, NODATA per naam+type; referral rank answer ko overwrite nahi karta; injected clock.
5. Demo: npx vitest run test/cache.test.ts
6. Interviewer next: serve-stale kya hai? LRU vs insertion-order eviction?
1. Concept: stub clients (nslookup, OS) RD=1 ke saath recursive resolver se poochte hain.
2. Project need: apna resolver real tools se use karna, bina duniya ke liye open resolver bane.
3. Code/API: server.ts DnsServer.listen, handle, isLoopback, stats; index.ts ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK.
4. Detail: FORMERR/NOTIMP/QR-drop rules, TC above 512, UDP + TCP same port.
5. Demo: $env:PORT=53; npm start; nslookup example.com. 127.0.0.1 (Windows nslookup -port ignore karta hai)
6. Interviewer next: open resolver amplification kaise kaam karta hai? Rate limiting kahan lagaoge?

learning_path.concept: Testing a network protocol without the network
steps: 1. Concept: fake authoritative servers in-process, fixture zones, aur ek route hook IP -> loopback port.
2. Project need: tests deterministic aur offline; misbehaviour (drop, garbage, spoof, poison, lame) chahiye jo real internet par nahi bana sakte.
3. Code/API: test/fakenet.ts FakeServer (answer, hook, log), FakeNet.route; test/fixtures.ts buildNet; Resolver option route.
4. Detail: UDP aur TCP same port; documentation IPs; opt-in live test LIVE_DNS=1 real roots ke saath, aur mutation checks se tests ki taakat.
5. Demo: npm test ; LIVE_DNS=1 npx vitest run test/live.test.ts
6. Interviewer next: mutation check jo koi test na pakde uska kya matlab? Equivalent mutant kya hai?
